summary: Verified bug fix for audio upload on WEB platform. (1) Reproduced original bug via page.evaluate with the RN FormData shape { uri, name, type } — backend returned exactly the reported 422 error: 'Value error, Expected UploadFile, received: <class \'str\'>, input: [object Object]'. (2) Verified fix in /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts uploadAnalysis(): Platform.OS==='web' branch fetches URI, converts to Blob, wraps in File, and appends to FormData — POST /api/analyses returned 200 with full analysis payload (id, mfcc_mean len=13, intonation=37.7, clarity=93.6, overall=65.7, ai_feedback 1251 chars, transcript string). (3) UI E2E: login as siswa via [data-testid=login-submit-btn] → /home shows student-home-record-btn → /record shows record-start-btn, record-timer, record-close-btn. (4) Navigated to /result/{new_id}: result-intonation-card, result-clarity-card, result-transcript, result-ai-feedback, result-new-recording-btn all PRESENT with real values rendered. (5) Backend regression: pytest 28/28 passed in 17.5s (auth, analyses upload/history/get/permissions, materials seeding, teacher stats/students/history).
critical_code_review_comments: client.ts uploadAnalysis uses require('react-native') inside an async function; acceptable but could be hoisted as top-level import to avoid per-call cost.

In record.tsx the recorded audio is m4a on native, but the on-web recording flow was not exercised (headless Playwright cannot grant mic); relies on expo-audio producing a fetchable URI on web. Fix code path itself is verified independently via evaluate.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix location: /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts lines 76-101. On web, do NOT append { uri, name, type }; instead fetch(uri) → blob() → new File([blob], filename, {type}) → form.append('file', file, filename). Verified by direct fetch inside page.evaluate at the app origin (same as production). Backend accepts multipart 'file' field on POST /api/analyses?title=...; guru gets 403 on upload (siswa-only). Test bug-shape by appending a plain JS object as 'file' → backend responds with the exact reported 422.
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: React Native's FormData on Web (React Native Web) serializes the RN-specific { uri, name, type } object via toString(), producing the literal string '[object Object]'. FastAPI's UploadFile validator then sees a str instead of a file and returns 422 'Expected UploadFile, received: <class str>'. REPRO: append({uri,name,type}) to FormData in a browser → POST → 422 with input '[object Object]' (confirmed live). FIX: on Platform.OS==='web', fetch(uri) → .blob() → new File([blob], filename, {type}) then form.append('file', file, filename); native branch keeps the RN shape which iOS/Android FormData understands. MITIGATION VERIFIED: 200 OK with valid analysis payload from real File; result screen renders all fields.
